items.title: Beginners Wheel - Mondays - 6 to 9 pm - 6 Classes
items.excerpt:
Mondays - November 2 to December 7, 2026

  • 6 Classes

  • 3 Hours / Class

Skill Level:

Beginners - Students who have never touched clay or for students who have taken one wheel class before.

Description:

Want to learn how to work clay on a Pottery wheel? Our teachers are some of the finest Artists and are very passionate about teaching. During these six classes of instructor led training, we will teach basics of Pottery that includes how to use a Pottery wheel, make functional forms like Cups, Bowls, Plates, Vases etc.

If you have never worked with clay or want to try it out for fun or have taken a class long time ago and want to get back or take Pottery seriously, this is the class to get started with.

Experience “Learning Excellence” at Vortex Pottery and see the difference in Quality.

Vortex Pottery’s core is “Learning Excellence” and we have modeled everything in the studio around this core. We spend one on one time and customize the learning for each student. As a result you will learn better, faster and do not pick up inefficiencies. You will do the best if you practice outside class hours. Hence we provide 24 Hours studio access. Students who practice outside class hours have seen tremendous progress and we encourage you to do so.

** IMPORTANT ** Students to bring the following:

  1. Beginners Pottery Wheel Tool Kit similar to the one from Amazon listed in the link below. If this tool kit listed is out of stock or not available anymore, any alternative Beginners Pottery Wheel Tool kit that is suggested works.

    Beginners Pottery Wheel Tool Kit

    Similar tool kits are available at other Art supply stores like Blick Art Materials, Michaels, Seattle Pottery Supply etc.

  2. Apron

  3. Hand Towel

  4. 16 Oz empty Yogurt Container to store your tools in the studio.

Instructor: Sudhi Tirnahalli

Sudhi has been an artist all his life. A classical musician, Calligraphist and more than two decades ago, he touched clay and has never looked back. He envisioned a Pottery studio built around “Learning Excellence” and his passion to teach. That resulted in Vortex Pottery. He is the Potter, Teacher, Founder & Owner of Vortex Pottery. He has taught pottery to thousands of students across the world and in many studios. The experience and his specialization in building curriculum, Skill Development and Competency Building - all these elements have helped him put together excellent learning programs at Vortex Pottery.

He has been a Speaker/Presenter at NCECA Conferences (National Council for Education in Ceramic Arts), the biggest clay conference in the world that brings in 7000+ Clay Artists together every year from many countries. He was also on the Board of Washington Clay Art Association which is one of the oldest Clay Art Associations in the country helping Artists/Clay organizations come together. His passion for learning shows in the classes he teaches.

OTHER DETAILS:

If you miss a class, there will be NO make up class. But we will try and go over missed topics again in the next class.

Price Includes first bag of Clay, Glazes and Bisque Firing to Cone 04 and Glaze Firing to Cone 6 in Electric Kilns.

1 class a week for 3 hours. You will have 24 hours Studio Access to practice except during Hours of maintenance, repairs, events etc.

Granite Calimpong received a BFA in Interdisciplinary Computing in the Arts and Music from UCSD in 2007 and completed his MFA in Sculpture at the University of Washington in 2019. While a graduate student at UW he explored perception and various visual phenomena associated with illusions through the use of Clay, wood, glass, photography, and metal. He has his studio in Seattle where he continues to explore. Calimpong has had solo exhibitions at Traver Gallery in Seattle and at the Jam Factory in Adelaide, Australia. items.title: Hand Sculpture - Wednesdays - 6 To 9 pm - 6 Classes
items.excerpt:
Wednesdays - November 4 to December 9, 2026

  • 6 Classes

  • 3 Hours / Class

Skill Level:

All Levels - Beginners who have never done hand building or sculpture and for students with any level of Experience in Hand building or sculpture.

There will be NO Pottery Wheel work in this class.

Description:

Our hands are very Powerful in many ways-

Hands feel - humans, animals, birds, creatures, materials, pressure, temperature etc.

Hands express - happiness, anger, love, emotions etc.

Hands - protect, build, help and uplift.

Its time for us to sculpt hands with our own hands. While learning basic techniques of hand-building, we will focus understanding the anatomy of a hand and sculpting it. Sandra Farmer is a sculpting genius and her work is stunning. Whether you are a beginner, intermediate or advanced hand builder / sculptor, you will love this class. Let us thank our hands for all it does for us.

Experience “Learning Excellence” at Vortex Pottery and see the difference in Quality.

Vortex Pottery’s core is “Learning Excellence” and we have modeled everything in the studio around this core. We spend one on one time and customize the learning for each student. As a result you will learn better, faster and do not pick up inefficiencies. You will do the best if you practice outside class hours. Hence we provide 24 Hours studio access.   2. Apron

  3. Hand Towel

  4. 16 Oz empty Yogurt Container to store your tools in the studio.

Instructor: Sandra Farmer

Sandra Farmer is a champion in teaching with more than three decades of teaching experience with hand-building & Sculpture. She earned her BFA in Crafts with a focus in Ceramics and a Bachelor of Interdisplinary Studies in Pre-Art Therapy from Virginia Commonwealth University in 2002. Farmer focuses on figurative ceramics and mixed media. She has been teaching ceramics and art for the past 20 years at various studios and institutions including the Children’s Museum of Richmond, VA, The Seattle Art Museum, The Children’s Museum in Seattle, Kirkland Arts Center(Kirkland, WA), Redmond Clay Studio (Redmond, WA) and Moshier Community Arts Center (Burien, WA). She has exhibited her work locally and nationally.
